title: Trace provenance policy engine and just-in-time access for observability
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Implement a policy-driven provenance layer for trace/span metadata and a just-in-time (JIT) access flow for querying sensitive observability data. Objective: enable fine-grained redaction & retention enforcement at query-time, provide a tamper-evident access log for all cross-tenant/role lookups, and deliver dashboard/alerting changes so SREs and engineers can reason about visibility and cost. This ticket covers the server-side policy engine, trace attribute escrow schema, query-time enforcement hooks, and the initial Console integration for access requests and audit viewing.
background: Current problem: traces and logs include rich attributes (user ids, email hashes, request headers) that can be PII or regulated. We already have tenant-scoped retention and bulk redaction jobs, but: 1) ad-hoc queries (SRE debugging, on-call) can surface sensitive fields; 2) cross-team access lacks just-in-time approvals and fine-grained provenance; 3) audits are fragmented between DB access logs and ad-hoc query tools. Legal wants tamper-evident provenance for compliance audits. Product requires minimal blast radius for debugging workflows while preserving SLO for latency/alerts.
technical_approach: Add a lightweight policy engine that evaluates rules (field-level allow/deny/transform) against trace/span metadata at query-time. Policies are tenant-scoped with optional role overrides.

Introduce an escrow layer for sensitive trace attributes: store originals in an encrypted, access-controlled store (escrow) and return redacted values by default; retrieval requires JIT approval or an allow-rule.

Instrument query path with tracing hooks: before returning spans, run policy evaluation -> either redact/obfuscate/return escrow reference -> record audit entry with requestor, policy-id, reason, and nonce.
Integrate RBAC + JIT flow: Console and API can trigger a short-lived approval token (approved by owner/service-account or auto-approvals based on policy). Tokens are scoped and logged.
Retention enforcement: mark escrowed attributes with independent retention TTL; compaction worker will purge escrow when both trace TTL and escrow TTL expire or on legal-hold override.

Dashboarding: add observability dashboards (latency & error dashboards) with visibility into percent of queries that returned escrowed fields, average policy evaluation latency, and audit log volume to detect abuse and cost regressions.
Performance: target <1ms added p50 latency for policy evaluation in the hot path; fallback to background redaction for very large batch exports.
APIs: add admin APIs to list policies, request JIT tokens, and review audit entries. All APIs require mTLS internally and E2E request tracing for correlation.
Migration: start with traces only (span tags), then extend to logs/metrics labels in follow-ups.
tasks: Design policy DSL and validation rules (Confluence: /doc/observability/provenance-policy-dsl)
Implement policy engine core and policy store (KVS-backed with versioning)
Add escrow store integration (KMS-wrapped objects, S3/GCS backing; create deletion hooks)
Hook policy evaluation into trace query path (runtime change + unit/e2e tests)
Build JIT approval flow in Console + API endpoints (UI mockups in Drive)
Add audit log schema and immutable append-only pipeline (stream to dedicated topic)
Create dashboards and alerts for policy evaluation latency and escrow usage
Write migration and rollback plan; document legal-hold semantics
Security review and threat model update
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine deployed behind feature flag and exercised by unit + integration tests
Escrow store encrypts attributes at rest and supports deletion-by-ttl; deletion tested end-to-end
Query path records audit entries for every access to escrowed attributes with requester identity and policy id
JIT approval token flow works end-to-end in Console and API and is time-limited and scoped
Dashboard surfaces <2s spikes in policy eval latency and percent of results containing escrowed fields
Performance impact on common trace queries is <1ms p50 and <5ms p95 when feature flag on for default policy
Security review completed and signed off by Security org
